articles.title: CITIZENLAB DETAILS NEW SPYWARE TRIGGERED BY ONLINE ADVERTISING
articles.summary: Discover-Tech, an Israeli firm presenting itself as an ad vendor, displayed 442 million ads on more than 120,000 websites and apps, including the BBC, The New York Times, and Duolingo. Some of those ads carried zero-click spyware that infected phones and computers simply by appearing on screen, with targets ranging from Al Jazeera journalists to NATO and NVIDIA staff. It is the first confirmed case of government-backed zero-click spyware delivered through online ads. Google has since blocked Discover-Tech from its ad platforms.

articles.title: HOW TO PITCH LOCAL NEWSROOMS IN THE US
articles.summary: Local news pitches are more effective when they target the right journalist, demonstrate a clear community impact, and provide everything needed to produce the story. Local newsrooms have declined by 81% since 2002, making relevant, ready-to-use pitches especially important. Start by reviewing journalists' recent coverage, then contact assignment editors at TV stations or editors at print and digital outlets when appropriate. Tailor pitches to the format: print needs a clear story and supporting data, TV needs visuals and local people to interview, and radio needs an available guest who can speak. Include a timely local angle, relevant data, quotes, visuals, and event details, and send the pitch before the newsroom's morning planning meeting.

articles.title: WHY BRANDS NEED TO FUEL A LIFE, NOT FILL A FEED
articles.summary: Pinterest reports that 40% of Gen Z wish social media had never been invented and 63% intentionally unplug. Design campaigns that drive real-world action rather than endless scrolling. Show how a product fits into the audience's desired lifestyle instead of making the product the hero. Turn inspiration into action with personalized recommendations and specific next steps such as shopping lists or linked outfits. Remove friction with tools that help people follow through.

articles.title: THE ART OF BRAND MERCH
articles.summary: People wear merch to say something about themselves, not to promote a company. A logo on a T-shirt or water bottle asks customers to carry a message without giving them a reason, and only works when the logo already means something. Strong merch does one of three jobs. It signals belonging through a recognizable color or shape, sells more product by being designed around how that product gets used, or lets in people who can't yet afford the core product.

HOW LONG SHOULD A REEL BE? UNDER 3 MINUTES ON INSTAGRAM, LONGER ON TIKTOK
articles.summary: Video length barely matters on Instagram until the 3-minute mark, where recommendations to new audiences stop. Reels from 10 seconds to 3 minutes all perform within 2% of each creator's median, while longer ones fall to 0.91x. TikTok rewards length instead, with 3-to-10-minute videos earning 1.22x and beating the same creator's 10-to-19-second clips for 68% of creators.
